shortDescription: Financial technology firm Revolut has received approval from Argentina's central bank to acquire Banco Cetelem Argentina S.A. from BNP Paribas Personal Finance, the company said in a statement on Thursday as it continues its expansion into Latin America.

children: Financial technology firm Revolut has received approval from Argentina's central bank to acquire Banco Cetelem Argentina S.A. from BNP Paribas Personal Finance, the company said in a statement on Thursday as it continues its expansion into Latin America.
Banco Cetelem will be renamed Revolut Bank Argentina and Agustin Danza will be appointed as its CEO, Revolut said.

The bank will operate as a regulated entity but will not initially offer public-facing products or services and will focus on fulfilling regulatory and operational requirements before a future market launch.
More than 150,000 consumers registered on Revolut's wait list in Argentina, the company said.
Revolut also secured its banking license in Colombia earlier this month, where it plans to being operations in 2027. The company said some 200,000 people have joined its waiting list in Colombia.
In early September, Revolut also received conditional approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national bank charter, targeting a 2027 launch.
The fintech firm entered the Mexican market in January and already has over 1 million users in the country.
Revolut serves more than 80 million customers worldwide and operates as a licensed bank in the UK, Mexico, Australia and across Europe.
